title: An Orca Is Never Only an Orca
truthCore: An Orca is a living individual inside social, acoustic, food-web and place relationships. A source-reported occurrence can support a bounded statement about one reported record; it does not by itself establish range, abundance, trend or ecosystem condition.
audienceJob: Distinguish evidence from interpretation while feeling the wider living system around one animal.

title: What Depends on What? Bee → Pollination → Food
truthCore: Many crop plants depend at least partly on animal pollination. Bees are important pollinators, but pollination is performed by many animal groups and not all food production depends on bees. Apple is the bounded production example for the first vertical slice: the story shows how multiple bee groups contribute to apple pollination without turning this into an all-food or all-bees claim.
audienceJob: Understand one visible dependency chain without turning a complex food system into a false universal claim.

sourceRefs.label: FAO — Global Action on Pollination Services for Sustainable Agriculture
sourceRefs.scope: pollination importance, crop dependence and multiple pollinator groups

sourceRefs.label: Garratt et al. — Apple pollination: demand depends on variety and supply depends on pollinator identity
sourceRefs.scope: bounded apple example across four commercial UK varieties and four pollinator guilds

title: Oslofjorden: One Place, Many Systems
truthCore: Oslofjorden is not one condition or score. Different parts, time periods, species and pressure layers can show different signals. 4PLANET should connect bounded source layers while keeping coverage, time, uncertainty and causal limits visible.
audienceJob: See one familiar place as a changing living system without mistaking partial observations for total condition or causal proof.
